body.p: Claim 1-20 are currently pending and at issue herein. Claims 1-15 stand rejected, and claims 16-20 stand withdrawn in view of a requirement for restriction made final. By this paper, no claims have been amended, added, or canceled. In light of the arguments that follow, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of all outstanding grounds of rejection and allowance of the application.

On page 4 of the Office Action, the different plugin types were identified as invoking means-plus-function treatment according to 35 U.S.C. § 112(f). Without acquiescing to the merits of this contention and to the extent that these limitations are treated as means-plus- function limitations, Applicant respectfully submits that the specification provides sufficient structure for these plugins in the form of algorithms describing their implementations in accordance with MPEP 2181(II)(B) ("For a computer-implemented 35 U.S.C. 112(f) claim limitation, the specification must disclose an algorithm for performing the claimed specific computer function ....").
Claims 1-15 stand rejected under as being anticipated by Artemiadis (U.S. Publication No. 2020/0057498). Applicant respectfully traverses this ground of rejection and requests withdrawal of same.

In the rejection, the Office alleges that the limitation of "a framework configured to execute an extensible architecture" "merely describes the portions of software used to perform the functions of the claim." Office Action, page 6. Applicants respectfully disagree because the contention is too simplistic and fails to give meaning to all words used in the claim. In particular, the framework is described as "an extensible architecture." For software, extensibility is known in the art to refer to the ability to add or modify functionalities of a software framework without making large changes to the core codebase. See, e.g., Specification, [0051]-[0052] ("[T]he core program 160 within the architecture of the framework 100 is responsible for managing all of the plugins, devices, and types within the current implementation. [.. .] The core program manages all connections between the plugins
by adding them to the relevant plugin and extension point lists based on the IDs provided within the definition file.").

In this regard, Applicant is not trying to read limitations from the specification into the claim, and instead, Applicant respectfully submits that the term "extensible" when used in the claim limitation of "extensible architecture" must be given appropriate weight and meaning. The rejection makes no argument regarding how the software of Artemiadis is extensible in anyway that would be understood by a person of ordinary skill in the art. Indeed, Artemiadis does not disclose, teach, or suggest any extensibility of the software controlling the disclosed system (200), and such extensibility and the software platform in general is not the focus of Artemiadis's disclosure. Instead, Artemiadis is directed to "a hybrid BCI system . .. which combines EEG signals and joystick input." See [0030]. Nothing about this focus explicitly or implicitly discloses an extensible architecture.

Because Artemiadis does not disclose "a framework configured to execute an extensible architecture," Artemiadis cannot anticipate claim 1 or its dependent claims. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this ground of rejection for at least this reason.

In addition, Artemiadis fails to disclose that "the extensible architecture is configured to extend to at least one further EEG device plugin associated with a different set of EEG electrodes" as recited in claim 1. Thus, Artemiadis does not anticipate claim 1 or its dependent claims for this additional reason.

In the rejection, Artemiadis is cited as disclosing a plurality of robotic devices (212), such as rotorcraft. Office Action, page 9. However, the robotic devices (212) are the object controlled using the brain control interface, not a different EEG device plugin associated with a different set of EEG electrodes. Artemiadis does not disclose the possibility of different EEG device plugins because Artemiadis does not consider the use of different EEG devices having different sets of EEG electrodes. Instead, the software architecture of Artemiadis is designed to be used with a single EEG device having one set of EEG electrodes, and the specific EEG device utilized in the disclosure of Artemiadis was Brain Products ActiCHamp amplifier system using 64 electrodes placed according to the 10/20 International system. See [0038]. Again, Artemiadis is not explicitly or implicitly directed to an extensible framework but rather is directed to hybrid BCI system that utilizes EEG signals and a joystick input. It is not within
the scope of Artemiadis's disclosure to consider the use of different EEG devices because it is not relevant to the innovation that Artemiadis seeks to describe.

Because Artemiadis also fails to disclose an "extensible architecture [that] is configured to extend to at least one further EEG device plugin associated with a different set of EEG electrodes," Artemiadis also does not anticipate claim 1 for this reason, and Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this ground of rejection.

Still further, Applicant respectfully asserts that Artemiadis does not disclose a "plugin" as would be understood by a person of ordinary skill in the art from the context of the claim. Claim 1 requires each of "a first EEG device plugin," "an interpreter plugin," and "a first object control plugin." While Artemiadis may disclose software that interacts with an EEG device to interpret EEG signals to control an object, Artemiadis does not contain disclosure sufficient to describe any of such software as a "plugin" used in an "extensible architecture."

Like "extensible," Applicant respectfully submits that the term "plugin" has a meaning that is understood by those of ordinary skill in the art, which is a software component that adds a specific feature to an existing computer program. See Specification, [0020] ("According to the present disclosure the plugin is a bundle that adds functionality to an application through defined architecture for extensibility."). Such plugins allow for "third-party developers to build applications that are modular, customizable, and extensible." Id. Nothing in the disclosure of Artemiadis suggests that plugins were developed to interact with the EEG device, interpret EEG signals, or control an object. Rather, the disclosure of Artemiadis suggests software in which each of these aspects is incorporated into a non-extensible core program. Again, Applicant is not arguing that limitations of the specification should be imported into the claim but that the term "plugin" should be given its ordinary and customary meaning as would be understood by one of ordinary skill in the art.

As such, Applicant respectfully asserts that Artemiadis fails to anticipate claim 1 and its dependent claims for this additional reason, and withdrawal of this ground of rejection is respectfully requested.

The application is considered in good and proper form for allowance, and the Examiner is respectfully requested to pass this application to issue. If, in the opinion of the Examiner, a telephone conference would expedite the prosecution of the subject application, the Examiner is invited to call the undersigned attorney.
